parameters.label: Wiek uderzenia / granicy K-Pg
parameters.locator: sprain2018: Abstract; sprain2015: Abstract; renne2018: Abstract; renne2013: Abstract
parameters.notes: 40Ar/39Ar on sanidine of the IrZ-coal tephra within ~1 cm of the impact claystone (Hell Creek, Montana): 66.052 +/- 0.008 Ma (analytical) / +/- 0.043 Ma (full); range = value +/- 0.043. Independent impact-ejecta age: Chicxulub spherules (Gorgonilla) 66.051 +/- 0.031 Ma (renne2018). Earlier pooled value 66.043 +/- 0.010/0.043 Ma (sprain2015), consistent with renne2013 (impact and boundary synchronous within 32 kyr). Older values 64.98 Ma (swisher1992) and ~65.95 Ma (kuiper2008) reflect older calibrations and are superseded. U-Pb (Clyde et al. 2016) not verified here.

parameters.label: Wiek sferul wyrzutowych Chicxulub (Gorgonilla, Kolumbia)
parameters.locator: Abstract
parameters.notes: Weighted mean 40Ar/39Ar age of 25 fresh glassy spherules; +/- 0.031 Ma as stated in the abstract (uncertainty type not specified there).

parameters.label: Pora roku uderzenia
parameters.value: wiosna na półkuli północnej (jesień na południowej)
parameters.method: measured proxies: osteohistology + stable isotopes of fishes killed at Tanis (seasonal inference)
parameters.locator: during2022: Abstract and main text; depalma2021: Abstract
parameters.notes: during2022: boreal spring; depalma2021: boreal spring/summer. Both from the Tanis seiche deposit (~50 deg N paleolatitude). Time of day is not constrained by any source.

parameters.label: Średnica impaktora (skalowanie krateru / modele hydrokodowe)
parameters.locator: collins2020: SI Table 1, Fig. 2-3 captions, Methods; artemieva2017: Sect. 4; artemieva2009: Sect. 3
parameters.notes: Not measured: it is the size that reproduces the observed crater (transient cavity ~90-100 km, seismically constrained) for an assumed speed, angle and density. collins2020 (iSALE3D, 2630 kg/m3): at 20 km/s 12/13/14/16 km for 90/60/45/30 deg; at 12 km/s 16/17/18/21 km. Preferred 45-60 deg -> 13-18 km. artemieva2017: 12.2 km (60 deg, 18 km/s, 2600 kg/m3). artemieva2009: 12 km (90 deg), 14.4 km (45 deg), 16 km (30 deg) at 18 km/s. goderis2021 quotes ~12 km. Baseline 13 km = collins2020 60 deg / 20 km/s. Geochemical (Ir) estimates are smaller: see impactor.diameter_geochem.

parameters.label: Średnica impaktora z bilansu irydu (Ir)
parameters.method: scaling: global Ir inventory / chondritic Ir content / globally dispersed fraction
parameters.locator: alvarez1980: Abstract; artemieva2009: Sect. 2; desch2022: Introduction; paquay2008: Abstract
parameters.notes: alvarez1980: 10 +/- 4 km (four independent estimates). artemieva2009: global Ir 2.0-2.8e8 kg, Ir 500 ng/g, dispersed fraction 0.22-0.5 -> mass 0.8-2.5e15 kg -> 8-12 km at 2600 kg/m3, 'too small to produce the 180-200 km diameter crater'. desch2022: D ~ 10 km. paquay2008: Os-isotope estimate within 50% of Ir-based ones (value not read). Lower bound on impactor mass (assumes all Ir globally dispersed).

parameters.label: Masa impaktora
parameters.method: scaling: m = (4/3)*pi*r^3*rho from published r and rho
parameters.locator: collins2020: SI Table 1 (radii, density); artemieva2017: Sect. 4 (2,500 Gt stated)
parameters.notes: Computed here: collins2020 60 deg/20 km/s (r = 6.5 km, 2630 kg/m3) -> 3.0e15 kg; range from collins2020 90 deg/20 km/s (2.4e15) to 45 deg/12 km/s (8.0e15). artemieva2017 states 2,500 Gt (2.5e15 kg). Ir-based mass 0.8-2.5e15 kg (artemieva2009). collins2020: for a given impactor mass the results are insensitive to the assumed density.

parameters.label: Typ / skład impaktora
parameters.value: asteroida typu węglistego (chondryt węglisty; najzgodniejszy z CM lub CR)
parameters.method: measured: Ru and Cr isotopes, PGE ratios, fossil meteorite in K-Pg clay (interpretation of measurements)
parameters.locator: fischergodde2024: Abstract; shukolyukov1998: Abstract; kyte1998: Abstract; desch2022: 'Geochemical arguments'
parameters.notes: Carbonaceous (CC-type) affinity from independent isotopic systems (Ru: carbonaceous-type asteroid formed beyond Jupiter's orbit; Cr: carbonaceous-chondrite type). Subtype debated: fossil meteorite allows CV/CO/CR/possibly CM, not CI; e54Cr argues CM-like (CR/CH/CB identical); PGE favour CM or CO, rule out CI (all as summarised by desch2022). Comet origin disfavoured (Ir budget, Ru isotopes).

parameters.label: Gęstość objętościowa impaktora
parameters.locator: collins2020: SI Table 1, Methods; artemieva2009: Sect. 3; christeson2009: Table 1; macke2011: Abstract
parameters.notes: Real density unknown (collins2020 Methods: bulk porosity 'undetermined'). Model values: 2600 (artemieva2009/2017; 'typical for large asteroids with 20-30% porosity'), 2630/2650 (collins2020, internally inconsistent), 2680 (christeson2009). Lower bound 2385 computed from collins2020's statement that Murchison (CM2) bulk density is ~10% below 2650. macke2011: CM/CR meteorites average ~23% porosity. Asteroid-scale macroporosity (rubble pile) could lower bulk density further - speculation, no Chicxulub-specific constraint.

parameters.label: Prędkość uderzenia
parameters.method: scaling: statistical Earth-impact speed distribution (no Chicxulub-specific measurement)
parameters.locator: collins2020: Results ('Numerical simulation results', paragraph after Fig. 5), Methods; artemieva2017: Sect. 4; pierazzo1998: Abstract
parameters.notes: No observation constrains the Chicxulub impact speed. collins2020: 20 km/s is 'close to Earth's mean and median asteroid impact speed' (citing Le Feuvre & Wieczorek 2011); ~25% of impacts are <15 km/s; minimum = escape velocity 11.2 km/s; 12 km/s runs used for computational expediency. Models: 18 km/s (artemieva2009/2017), 20 km/s asteroid / 50 km/s comet (pierazzo1998). Comet-speed cases disfavoured by composition (see impactor.type).

parameters.label: Kąt uderzenia (od poziomu)
parameters.locator: collins2020: Abstract, Fig. 5, 'Comparison with observations'; morgan2006: Abstract; schultz1996: Abstract
parameters.notes: collins2020: 45-60 deg (preferred ~60 deg) from 3D iSALE runs compared with offsets of the peak-ring centre and mantle-uplift centre; <30 deg ruled out. morgan2006: >45 deg (shocked quartz, continuous proximal ejecta). artemieva2009 used 45 deg as statistically most likely; artemieva2017 used 60 +/- 10 deg. Opposing: schultz1996 20-30 deg. Statistics: 1/4 of impacts steeper than 60 deg, 1/15 steeper than 75 deg (collins2020); 50% between 30 and 60 deg (artemieva2017).

parameters.label: Azymut nadejścia impaktora (skąd przyleciał; od N zgodnie z ruchem wskazówek zegara)
parameters.locator: collins2020: 'Comparison with observations', Fig. 1, SI Fig. 1; schultz1996: Abstract; morgan2006: Abstract
parameters.notes: collins2020 states only 'northeast-to-southwest' (arrival from the NE). 45 deg is the cardinal NE value, not a fitted azimuth; range 0-90 = NE quadrant. Bearings computed here from collins2020 coordinates: mantle-uplift centre ~10 km at ~6 deg (uprange); peak-ring / gravity-high centre ~7.6 km at ~223 deg (downrange, i.e. uprange ~43 deg). artemieva2017 uses downrange SW. Opposing: schultz1996 from the SE (~135 deg, toward NW); morgan2006 possible uprange SE +/- 45 deg; Hildebrand et al. 1998 (LPSC abstract, not peer-reviewed; cited by collins2020) from the SW. gulick2008: pre-impact target heterogeneity strongly shapes the asymmetry, so azimuth inferred from structure is uncertain.

parameters.label: Energia kinetyczna uderzenia (szacunki z literatury)
parameters.method: scaling: E = 0.5*m*v^2 from published m (or r, rho) and v; plus explicit published range (pope1997)
parameters.locator: collins2020: SI Table 1; artemieva2017: Sect. 4; artemieva2009: Sect. 3; pope1997: Abstract
parameters.notes: Computed here from published scenario parameters: collins2020 60 deg/20 km/s 6.05e23 J (baseline); 45 deg/20 km/s 7.6e23; 60 deg/12 km/s 4.9e23; 90 deg 4.1-4.8e23; 30 deg 0.9-1.1e24 J. artemieva2017 (2,500 Gt, 18 km/s) 4.05e23 J; artemieva2009 45 deg/18 km/s 6.6e23 J. Explicit older estimate: pope1997 0.7-3.4e31 erg = 0.7-3.4e24 J. Modern seismically/drilling-constrained scenarios at 45-60 deg cluster at ~5-8e23 J.

parameters.label: Energia kinetyczna w megatonach TNT
parameters.method: scaling: E[J] / 4.184e15 J per Mt TNT
parameters.locator: derived from energy.kinetic_literature
parameters.notes: Unit conversion of energy.kinetic_literature (1 Mt TNT = 4.184e15 J).

parameters.label: Głębokość wody w rejonie uderzenia (wartość modelowa; rampa węglanowa)
parameters.locator: artemieva2017: Sect. 4 (last paragraph); artemieva2009: Sect. 3; kaskes2023: Discussion (rim-wave tsunami paragraph); gulick2019: 'Postimpact Resurge, Settling, Seiches, and Tsunami'
parameters.notes: Ground-zero depth is NOT fixed in any source read. Target was a carbonate ramp deepening to the NE (gulick2008, via others). kaskes2023: <50 m south of the impact site and 100-2,000 m within the impacted area. artemieva2017: 'fairly shallow sea' over northern Yucatan, 'up to 1.5 km deep to the northeast of the point of impact', modelled as a water layer = R/4 (~1.5 km) - the 1500 m value is this modelled upper case, NOT a measured ground-zero depth. artemieva2009: >2 km water in N/NE quadrant (one run with 3 km water). range2022: 'struck in shallow water'. A simulation should use a spatially varying ramp.

parameters.label: Głębokość wody na szelfie na S od miejsca uderzenia
parameters.method: reconstruction (seismic + regional stratigraphy) as cited by kaskes2023
parameters.locator: Discussion (rim-wave tsunami paragraph)
parameters.notes: Upper bound '<50 m' south of the impact site (citing gulick2008 and Snedden & Galloway 2019).

parameters.label: Maksymalna głębokość wody w sektorze NE
parameters.method: reconstruction from seismic data (gulick2008) as cited
parameters.locator: artemieva2009: Sect. 3; artemieva2017: Sect. 4; gulick2019: 'Postimpact Resurge...'; kaskes2023: Discussion
parameters.notes: artemieva2009: '>2 km water' in N/NE quadrant; artemieva2017: 'up to 1.5 km'; gulick2019: depths 'reaching ~2 km' via the NNE rim gap (refs Sanford et al. 2016, gulick2008); kaskes2023: up to 2,000 m. All trace back to gulick2008, which was not read in full.

parameters.label: Miąższość pokrywy osadowej (węglany + ewaporaty)
parameters.locator: collins2020: Fig. 2 caption, Results; artemieva2017: Sect. 4; kring2004: Abstract
parameters.notes: ~3 km 'average thickness of sedimentary rocks at Chicxulub' (collins2020; '>3-km-thick' in text); '3 km-thick carbonate platform' (kring2004). Lateral variation: 3.8 +/- 0.2 km west of centre (Bell et al. 2004 via artemieva2017), >=2.8 km to the south (well Y-2), 3.3-3.5 km adopted for SW. Models use 3 km (christeson2009, artemieva2009).

parameters.label: Udział ewaporatów (anhydryt/gips) w pokrywie osadowej
parameters.method: measured (drill cores, wells) + model:artemieva2017 two-layer assumption
parameters.locator: gulick2019: Introduction and 'Excavation Stage'; artemieva2017: Sect. 4
parameters.notes: gulick2019: target sediments contained 30-50% evaporites; Yaxcopoil-1 slump block 27% anhydrite and >70% carbonates; deeper target possibly 49-60% anhydrite. artemieva2017: upper half 25% anhydrite / 75% calcite, lower half 60% anhydrite / 40% calcite; 0.425 = mean of the two halves (computed here). Contested because the M0077 suevite contains <1% evaporite (gulick2019), read either as efficient degassing or preferential export of non-porous evaporite clasts.

parameters.label: Udział węglanów (kalcyt/dolomit) w pokrywie osadowej
parameters.locator: as target.evaporite_fraction
parameters.notes: Computed as 1 - evaporite fraction; Yaxcopoil-1 >70% carbonates. Neglects minor siliciclastics/chert.

parameters.label: Grubość skorupy (do Moho, łącznie z pokrywą osadową)
parameters.method: model inputs informed by seismic Moho mapping
parameters.locator: collins2020: Methods; christeson2009: Sect. 3.2 and modelling paragraph; artemieva2009: Sect. 3
parameters.notes: collins2020: flat two-layer target with crustal thickness 33 km (sediments tracked with tracers, not a separate material). christeson2009 and artemieva2009: 3 km sediment + 30 km crystalline crust over mantle. Regional Moho dips W->E (christeson2009); the regional Moho depth number was not read in the text (their Fig. 4). Post-impact Moho upwarp 1.5-2 km at the centre.

parameters.label: Reprezentatywna gęstość celu do skalowania (skorupa granitowa)
parameters.locator: collins2020: SI Table 1 (crust reference density 2630; mantle 3310); artemieva2017: Sect. 2
parameters.notes: Crust modelled as granite (ANEOS) 2630 kg/m3 in collins2020 SI Table 1 (2650 in Methods text). artemieva2017: non-porous calcite target 2600, water-saturated porous calcite 2280 kg/m3.

parameters.label: Gęstość płaszcza (model)
parameters.locator: SI Table 1
parameters.notes: Dunite ANEOS reference density used in iSALE3D.

parameters.label: Szerokość geograficzna nominalnego środka krateru (współczesna)
parameters.method: measured: geometric centre of the rim from horizontal gravity gradient + cenote ring
parameters.locator: collins2020: Introduction, Fig. 1
parameters.notes: Nominal centre 21.29 N, 89.53 W. Other centres: central gravity high / annular low 21.24 N, 89.58 W (several km WSW); maximum mantle uplift 21.38 N, 89.52 W (~10 km NNE).

parameters.label: Długość geograficzna nominalnego środka krateru (współczesna)
parameters.locator: collins2020: Introduction, Fig. 1
parameters.notes: West longitude is negative.

parameters.label: Średnica krateru końcowego
parameters.locator: hildebrand1995: Abstract; christeson2009: Sect. 2; gulick2019: Introduction; gulick2013: Abstract
parameters.notes: ~180 km (hildebrand1991, hildebrand1995 - same rim definition as the nominal centre); 180-200 km (christeson2009, artemieva2009); ~200 km (gulick2019, ormo2021). Value depends on which ring is called the rim (gulick2013: inner rim at 70-85 km radius, outer ring faults at 70-130 km radius).

parameters.label: Średnica krateru przejściowego
parameters.locator: morgan1997: Abstract; gulick2013: Abstract; artemieva2009: Sect. 3; collins2020: SI Table 1
parameters.notes: ~100 km (morgan1997; gulick2013: 50 km radius; gulick2019 Fig. 2B); 90-100 km target in artemieva2009; 72-91 km in coarse iSALE3D runs (collins2020). Forms 'within 10 s' (gulick2013), 'within tens of seconds' (gulick2019), 'in the first minute' (collins2020).

parameters.label: Paleoszerokość miejsca uderzenia (66 Ma)
parameters.method: scaling: geocentric axial dipole tan(I) = 2 tan(lat) applied to inclination ~-46 deg
parameters.locator: gulick2019: Observations (paleomagnetism paragraph)
parameters.notes: gulick2019 gives the expected (and in Units 3/2C observed) inclination ~-46 deg during chron C29r. Paleolatitude computed here assuming a geocentric axial dipole; cross-check with the paleogeography thread (plate reconstruction).

positions.claim: Steep impact 45-60 deg (preferred ~60 deg), arriving from the NE (downrange SW); 3D iSALE runs vs offsets of peak-ring and mantle-uplift centres; <30 deg ruled out
Low-angle impact 20-30 deg from the SE toward the NW, from geophysical asymmetries and ejecta/biotic patterns
High angle >45 deg; uprange possibly SE +/- 45 deg from shocked-quartz shock levels; overall near-symmetric distal ejecta
Crater asymmetry correlates with pre-existing undulations of the end-Cretaceous shelf, so trajectory cannot be read from structure alone

disagreements.assessment: A steep angle (>=45 deg) is supported by several independent lines (seismically imaged structure + 3D models, continuous peak ring, near-symmetric shocked-quartz/ejecta distribution). The azimuth is much weaker: collins2020's NE origin relies on attributing centre offsets to the trajectory, whereas gulick2008 shows that target heterogeneity (water depth, sediment thickness) also produces asymmetry, and morgan2006 tentatively points SE. Azimuth stays contested; NE is the best-supported published option.

disagreements.topic: Rozmiar impaktora: skalowanie krateru vs bilans irydu

positions.claim: Hydrocode/crater scaling: 12-18 km for 45-60 deg at 12-20 km/s (density ~2600-2630 kg/m3)
Ir mass balance: ~8-12 km (mass 0.8-2.5e15 kg); 10 +/- 4 km; Os isotopes within 50% of Ir-based values

disagreements.assessment: The approaches differ by ~1.2-1.8x in diameter (~2-6x in mass). artemieva2009 notes the Ir inventory is too small for a 180-200 km crater; explanations include lower Ir in the impactor, Ir retained near the crater, or Ir lost. Crater-based estimates are tied to geometry and preferred for energy; Ir-based ones are a lower bound on globally dispersed impactor mass.

positions.claim: Fragment of a tidally disrupted long-period comet (D ~ 7 km) can explain the event rate and carbonaceous composition
Asteroid strongly favoured: a comet would deliver ~4% of the observed Ir; CM/CR match; fragment numbers overestimated
Ru isotopes indicate a carbonaceous-type asteroid formed beyond Jupiter
Survival of a fossil meteorite favours a low (asteroidal) velocity

disagreements.assessment: Asteroid origin is strongly favoured by geochemistry (Ir budget, Ru and Cr isotopes, fossil meteorite); the comet hypothesis was rebutted in a Matters Arising and is not supported by the 2024 Ru data.

positions.claim: Carbonaceous-chondrite-type Cr isotope signature
Fossil meteorite allows CV/CO/CR/possibly CM, not CI; e54Cr argues CM-like; PGE favour CM or CO, rule out CI -> CM or CR overall

disagreements.assessment: CC affinity is robust; exact subtype (CM vs CR) unresolved. Primary e54Cr (Trinquier et al. 2006) and PGE (Goderis et al. 2013) papers were not opened; their content is taken from desch2022's summary.

positions.claim: Baptistina family breakup ~160 Myr ago is the probable (>90%) source
298 Baptistina is S-type-like (olivine/pyroxene, albedo ~20%), weakening the CM2/K-T link

disagreements.assessment: The Baptistina link is disfavoured by spectroscopy; the source region remains open (Ru data say only 'formed beyond Jupiter').

positions.claim: 64.98 +/- 0.05 Ma (melt rock), 65.01 +/- 0.08 Ma (Beloc tektites)
~65.95 Ma (astronomically calibrated FCs 28.201 Ma)
66.043 +/- 0.010/0.043 Ma; impact and boundary synchronous within 32 kyr
66.052 +/- 0.008/0.043 Ma (boundary tephra); 66.051 +/- 0.031 Ma (Chicxulub spherules)

disagreements.assessment: Differences are dominated by standard/decay-constant calibration; current best ~66.05 Ma, full uncertainty ~+/-0.04 Ma. Irrelevant for the 24 h dynamics except as a label.

positions.claim: ~4-8e23 J for 45-90 deg scenarios constrained by the seismic transient cavity and drilling (derived from published m, v)

disagreements.assessment: Modern hydrocode scenarios tied to the seismically constrained transient cavity are preferred; pope1997 predates the 3D and drilling constraints. Shallow (30 deg) scenarios would need ~1e24 J but are disfavoured.

positions.claim: Fairly shallow sea; up to 1.5 km deep to the NE of the point of impact
>2 km water in the N/NE quadrant
<50 m south of the impact site; 100-2,000 m within the impacted area (carbonate ramp)
The asteroid struck in shallow water

disagreements.assessment: All trace back to gulick2008's seismic reconstruction (not read in full). Consensus: a ramp deepening to the NE, shallow to the S/SW; the ground-zero value is not fixed in the sources read.

positions.claim: Target sediments 30-50% evaporites; Yaxcopoil-1 block 27% anhydrite; deeper target possibly 49-60%
M0077 suevite contains <1% evaporite: either non-linear (more efficient) degassing or preferential export of non-porous evaporite clasts

disagreements.assessment: Evaporite fraction 0.3-0.5 is the working range; its fate matters for S release (gas thread), not for impactor kinematics.

openQuestions: Ground-zero water depth: no single published value read; gulick2008 full text (seismic paleobathymetry) and ormo2021 (d/H relation applied to Chicxulub) should be read to pin it down.
unverified lead: Renne et al. 2013 primary numerical values (K-Pg tephra ~66.043 Ma; Haiti tektite age) - full text not accessible; the boundary value is confirmed only via the sprain2015 abstract.

unverified lead: Clyde, W.C. et al. 2016, Earth Planet. Sci. Lett. 452:272-280, doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2016.07.041 - U-Pb age of the end-Cretaceous extinction (metadata confirmed via Crossref; abstract/values not accessed).
unverified lead: Le Feuvre, M. & Wieczorek, M.A. 2011, Icarus 214:1-20, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2011.03.010 - source of the ~20 km/s mean Earth impact speed; cited here only through collins2020.

unverified lead: Trinquier, A., Birck, J.-L., Allegre, C.J. 2006, Earth Planet. Sci. Lett. 241:780-788, doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2005.11.006 (e54Cr) and Goderis, S. et al. 2013, Geochim. Cosmochim. Acta 120:417-446, doi:10.1016/j.gca.2013.06.010 (PGE) - content used only via desch2022.

unverified lead: Morgan, J.V., Bralower, T.J., Brugger, J., Wunnemann, K. 2022, Nat. Rev. Earth Environ., doi:10.1038/s43017-022-00283-y - review likely to give consolidated impactor parameters; not accessed.
unverified lead: Nesvorny, D., Bottke, W.F., Marchi, S. 2021, Icarus 368:114621, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2021.114621 - share of dark primitive asteroids among K/Pg-scale impactors; abstract not read.
unverified lead: model set-up of range2022 (impactor size/speed, water depth used in iSALE) - full text not accessible.

Atmospheric entry duration: no Chicxulub-specific published number found (shuvalov2002 modelled the flight through the atmosphere, number not read). Compute in the simulation: t ~ h0/(v sin(theta)) -> ~6 s for h0 = 100 km, 20 km/s, 60 deg; ~2.5-17 s for h0 = 50-100 km, 12-20 km/s, 30-90 deg.
Impact time of day: unconstrained by any source.
Exact approach azimuth within the NE quadrant: collins2020 gives only 'from the northeast'; no fitted azimuth with uncertainty is published in the sources read.
Impactor macroporosity, shape and rotation: unknown; collins2020 states bulk porosity is undetermined.
Regional pre-impact Moho depth (christeson2009 Fig. 4) not extracted as a number; 33 km is a model input.
collins2020 internal inconsistency in impactor density (2630 vs 2650 kg/m3) - negligible for kinematics, note for reproducibility.
Paleolatitude 27.4 deg is a dipole-formula estimate from gulick2019's inclination; verify with a plate reconstruction (paleogeography thread).
paquay2008 Os-based K/Pg diameter value not read (full text inaccessible).
